text.brief: FBI agents arrested the Amerasia editor Philip Jaffe and five others in June 1945.
text.record: Agents had found hundreds of classified government documents in the magazine's New York office. Earlier warrantless entries by OSS officers and FBI agents weakened the case, and a grand jury declined to indict the diplomat John Service. Jaffe paid a fine of $2,500, and no one went to prison.
text.reading: The first China leak case failed on the defender's own procedure, and the failure fed a decade of suspicion that ruined careers more than it protected secrets. Bad process on a real breach produces both a free culprit and a purge.
text.gapText: Data Architecture. The defenders could not show how documents left their channels, and their own illegal entries spoiled the evidence.
text.fix: Log access to classified material by person and time, so a leak case rests on records rather than break-ins.
